recent_videos.title: The Detective Who Made a Deal With Death
recent_videos.description:
You owe Death an immortal man and she has given you the power to go and get him

- Solve a string of murders in your town
- Turn into La Sombra to fight the criminals
- Bring Death the one man who cannot die

Game is Mariachi Legends. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: Scientists Went Too Far And This Is What Came Out
recent_videos.description:
The thing you bred to feed the world is now a monster eating the whole lab

- It adapts and spreads room to room
- Use lab gear to slow it down
- Cut its tentacles & hit its weak spots
- Escape each floor before it mutates

Game is Demon Spore. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: A racing game with no speed limit played on a finger skateboard
recent_videos.description:
Race a tiny finger skateboard through cardboard tracks built across a childhood bedroom

- Replay and perfect your runs
- Earn medals, unlock new levels and abilities
- Flip, grind and perform big leaps

Game is STUNTBOOST. It's out on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: Every item you equip becomes a card in your deck
recent_videos.description:
Your gear is your deck in this dungeon card game

- Fight on a grid where position matters
- Every action is decided by a dice roll
- The dungeon changes each time you run it

Game is Lootdeck. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: Pixel art Devil May Cry where you have to kill your own mentor
recent_videos.description:
Your old master is heading for a gate that grants any wish and you have to kill him first

- Fast sword fights that test your timing
- Every frame of animation drawn by hand
- Story told in comic panels and cutscenes

Game is Last Ditch Effort. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: This Horror Game Watches Your Eyes Through Your Webcam
recent_videos.description:
Blink once and the monsters get to move.

- Descend into an abandoned lab full of monsters
- Scavenge what you can
- Every blink can change the world around you
- Make it out before your eyes give in

Game is DON'T BLINK. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: This Dragon Ball looking RPG is actually a brand new indie game
recent_videos.description:
Fight your way up a league of martial artists in this pixel art anime RPG

- Fight rivals with fast martial arts combos
- Charge your aura to fire energy attacks
- Rise through the Super Fighter League

Game is MythicTale. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: They Spent 8 Years Making Skyrim In Pixel Art
recent_videos.description:
Imagine Skyrim but every pixel was drawn by hand

- Explore a huge open world full of secrets
- Sneak into crypts, caves and houses
- Fight on a grid with quick time attacks
- Eight years in the making

Game is World of Anterra. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: A Game For People Who Still Want To Learn To Draw
recent_videos.description:
This solo dev made a game that teaches you how to draw

- Walk around a garden of statues and sketch them
- Real sculptures 3D scanned for accurate anatomy
- Dynamic lighting mode to practice shading

Game is Figure Drawing Garden. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: A Stealth Game Set in a World Where the Y2K Bug Actually Happened
recent_videos.description:
The Y2K bug hit and froze the world in the year 2000 and you're a spy sneaking through it

- Classic, deliberate stealth with visibility & noise detection
- Hand-crafted locations
- Hidden routes and more than one way in
- Non-lethal and lethal

Game is SeverLink. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: Celeste's Pixel Artist Is Making a Horror Farming RPG
recent_videos.description:
A farming life sim that is secretly a horror RPG, co-created by Celeste's pixel artist

- Fight through horrors
- Farm, craft, cook, and decorate your home
- Meet or date 10+ characters
- Original soundtrack by Disasterpeace

Game is Neverway. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

recent_videos.title: Sword duels in an adventure game hand animated like a 1980s Don Bluth film
recent_videos.description:
This is insane talent, and no GenAI! Kudos to the devs

- Explore forests and ruins, solve puzzles
- Sword fights built on dodging and stamina
- Quests raise your health and sword skill

Game is War of the Western Deep. You can wishlist it on Steam now.

In God of War (2018), Baldur spent the final moments of his life fighting the wrong person in an unforgettable Kratos vs Baldur rivalry. When The Stranger (Baldur) first knocks on Kratos's door in Midgard and says, "I thought you'd be bigger," most players assumed he was mocking the Ghost of Sparta... but hidden God of War lore reveals Odin never sent Baldur after Kratos at all. Instead, Baldur was tracking the last Giant hiding in Midgard: Kratos's deceased wife and Atreus's mother, Laufey the Just (Faye).

So if Kratos and Atreus were hidden for years inside Midgard's magical forest, how did Odin's best tracker suddenly find their home? In the very first minute of God of War 4, the golden handprint tree that Kratos chops down with the Leviathan Axe for Faye's funeral pyre was actually the final stave of Faye's protection spell. By cutting down that marked tree in the God of War opening scene, Kratos accidentally broke the magical barrier hiding them from the Aesir gods.

However, the God of War ending in Jötunheim changes everything. The Jötunheim prophecy mural proves that Faye foresaw every step of Kratos and Atreus's journey long before it happened. This raises the ultimate God of War theory leading into God of War Ragnarök: did Faye intentionally mark that exact protection tree for Kratos to cut down so Baldur would find them and force their journey to Jötunheim to begin? recent_videos.title: Why Video Game Cars Have NO Real Wheels!
recent_videos.description:
#gta5 ,#gtav ,#beamngdrive ,#forzahorizon5 ,#granturismo7 ,#gamephysics ,#gamedevelopment ,#gamingfacts ,#indiangaming ,#shorts 

Have you ever wondered how car physics in video games actually work behind the scenes? In this video, we expose the biggest secret in game development: almost every racing and open-world game... from Forza Horizon 5 and Gran Turismo 7 to GTA 5 (Grand Theft Auto V)... uses completely fake 3D wheels that never even touch the road!

When early game developers tried coding realistic car physics with solid 3D tires, they ran into a massive game engine bug. Because a physics engine only calculates 60 frames per second (60 FPS), a tire spinning at 200 km/h slightly clips inside the road between Frame 1 and Frame 2. The game physics engine misreads this tiny overlap as a massive collision, violently launching the car straight into the sky in games like Gran Turismo 7.

To fix this collision detection glitch, developers deleted physical wheels from the game code entirely. Inside the engine, your supercar is actually just a floating invisible hitbox (invisible dabba). Using a game dev technique called Raycasting, the car shoots four invisible lasers straight down from each corner accompanied by invisible suspension springs to detect bumps on the map, while the spinning tires you see on screen are just a fake 3D animation taped over those lasers.

recent_videos.title: How Hellblade Tricked Millions of Players! 🧠 | Dark Rot Secret Explained
recent_videos.description:
#hellblade ,#senuassacrifice ,#hellblade2 ,#dark ,#ninjatheory ,#gamingfacts ,#hindigaming ,#gamedesign ,#gaminglore ,#senua 

In Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice, developer Ninja Theory pulled off one of the greatest psychological tricks in video game design history by telling players a terrifying lie right at the start of the game. When a mysterious Dark Rot begins spreading up Senua's arm, the game issues a brutal permadeath warning: if you die too many times in combat, the Dark Rot will reach Senua's head, and your save files will be permanently deleted.

Because of this high stakes game mechanic, every single boss fight in Hellblade pushed players' heart rates to the limit, forcing gamers to dodge every attack as if their real lives depended on it. However, when curious players tested the Hellblade permadeath mechanic by intentionally dying over 50 times, they uncovered a shocking gaming secret—the save files were never deleted because permadeath code never existed in the game.

In the Hellblade story and lore, Senua suffers from severe psychosis, a mental health condition that makes the mind fear terrifying delusions that aren't even real. Instead of coding an actual save file deletion system, the developers used a fake Dark Rot warning to plant the exact same paranoia and anxiety inside the player's mind that Senua experiences every single second of her journey.

recent_videos.title: The Hidden Truth Behind Black Myth: Wukong’s First Trailer 🔥 | Game Science Story
recent_videos.description:
#blackmythwukonggameplay ,#wukong ,#gamescience ,#sunwukong ,#blackmythwukonggameplay ,#blackmythwukongtrailer ,#blackmyth ,#blackmythwukonggame ,#blackmythwukonghindi ,#actionrpg 

The first trailer of Black Myth: Wukong was never actually meant for gamers... it was a desperate cry for help and a secret recruitment job ad that changed gaming history forever.

For years, the global gaming industry believed that Asian studios could only produce cheap, pay-to-win mobile games. Frustrated with building greedy mobile titles and virtual casinos at Tencent, Feng Ji and a small group of passionate developers quit their jobs in 2014 to found Game Science. Their dream was to create a true AAA PC game and Action RPG rooted in Chinese mythology and the legendary tale of Sun Wukong (Journey to the West).

However, while developing Black Myth: Wukong, the tiny indie studio hit a massive wall: they were running out of money and developers, and no top-tier game dev wanted to risk their career on an unknown studio. Facing total project shutdown, Game Science poured everything they had left into a 13-minute Black Myth: Wukong gameplay demo and uploaded the first official trailer to the internet on August 20, 2020.

At the very end of that Black Myth: Wukong gameplay trailer, they placed a recruitment message asking Unreal Engine developers to apply. Feng Ji and his team only hoped to get 20 to 30 job applications. Instead, the Black Myth: Wukong trailer shook the entire video game industry within 24 hours... crossing 10 million (1 Crore) views and flooding Game Science with over 10,000+ developer resumes.

Exactly 4 years later, on August 20, 2024, that same small team released Black Myth: Wukong on PS5 and PC (Steam), shattering the Steam all-time single-player concurrent player record with over 2.4 million players. recent_videos.title: Mario’s Iconic Design Was Actually a "Jugaad"!
recent_videos.description:
#supermario ,#mario ,#nintendo ,#supermariobros ,#donkeykong ,#shigerumiyamoto ,#retrogaming ,#gamingfacts ,#videogamehistory ,#mariogame 

Did you know that the iconic Super Mario character design wasn't born out of a grand creative vision, but was actually a clever "jugaad" to beat 8-bit hardware limitations? In this video, we uncover the fascinating Super Mario origin story and video game history going all the way back to 1981 when legendary game developer Shigeru Miyamoto was designing a character for the classic Nintendo arcade game Donkey Kong.

Because the early gaming console hardware was so weak and limited to a tiny 16x16 pixel grid, animating a character's mouth and lips on a pixelated screen was impossible, so Miyamoto hid his mouth behind Mario's famous mustache. Similarly, animating moving hair while jumping in retro pixel art games was too difficult, which led to the creation of Mario's iconic red cap. Even Mario's big nose was a smart game design trick used to clearly show which direction the Nintendo mascot was facing and moving on screen.

Beyond the retro character design, we also reveal how Super Mario got his name. Originally named Jumpman in Donkey Kong, the character was renamed while Nintendo of America was operating out of a rented warehouse near Seattle (Tukwila, WA). When their real-life landlord, Mario Segale, showed up demanding rent, the Nintendo team noticed his striking resemblance and matching mustache to Jumpman, officially renaming the world's most famous video game character to Mario!

In this video I talk about how the series lost its identity — the tighter worlds, the real atmosphere, the defining mechanics that actually mattered, and the darker, more focused hero’s journey that made the older games hit so hard. Majora’s Mask in particular reminded me what was missing.

Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom might have sold millions, but they also marked the point where Zelda stopped feeling like Zelda.

If you still prefer the old formula, you’re not alone.
